articles.title: Sense and Sensibility film adaptation features rugged English countryside portrayal
articles.summary: The latest adaptation of Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility has drawn attention for its departure from traditional adaptations, opting instead for a more rugged and natural portrayal of...
articles.content: The latest adaptation of Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility has drawn attention for its departure from traditional adaptations, opting instead for a more rugged and natural portrayal of the English countryside. In contrast to previous versions, this film leans into the messy terrain and heartbreak that often accompany romance. Director Georgia Oakley's vision was clear: she wanted to create a raw and unbridled atmosphere that would allow viewers to fully immerse themselves in the story. To achieve this look, location manager Ian Hutchinson worked closely with Oakley to select filming locations that showcased the rustic beauty of England's countryside. As he noted, "you can really get into the rustic side of things", a sentiment that reflects the film's commitment to authenticity. While viewers may not be able to inherit grand estates or experience heartbreak at the hands of a dashing but untrustworthy suitor like John Willoughby, they can still visit the real-life locations where the film was shot. These sites offer a unique opportunity to step into the world of Sense and Sensibility and live out one's own period-drama fantasies. The five filming locations are scattered across England, each offering a glimpse into the lives of Austen's beloved characters. From extravagant estates to moody moorlands, these settings provide the perfect backdrop for romance, drama, and self-discovery. Whether you're a die-hard fan of Jane Austen or simply looking for a unique travel experience, these locations are sure to captivate and inspire, offering a chance to immerse oneself in the world of Sense and Sensibility like never before. The picturesque landscapes of England's Dorset region have been brought to life as the setting for the iconic novel Sense and Sensibility. Two separate estates in this area play a crucial role in recreating the idyllic world of Norland Park, where the story begins. Parnham Park is one such estate that has been transformed into the exterior grounds of Norland Park. This 139-acre historic property boasts an array of natural beauty, including ancient forests, rose gardens, and a serene spring-fed lake. The tranquil atmosphere makes it easy to see why Marianne would be heartbroken to leave this enchanting landscape behind. Visitors can experience firsthand the tranquility of Parnham Park by strolling through its manicured lawns or skipping stones across its fuchsia flower-framed pond. As they wander through the estate's pristine grounds, viewers are transported into a world where love and romance flourish amidst nature's splendor. Just 15 miles away from Parnham Park lies Kingston Russell House, which served as the interior of Norland Park and its main entrance in the film adaptation. This baroque-style mansion boasts an impressive Georgian facade with arched windows, creating a striking visual contrast against the earthy simplicity of Barton Cottage. For those looking to fully immerse themselves in the world of Sense and Sensibility, Kingston Russell House offers a unique opportunity to stay within its guest wing. Alternatively, visitors can explore the picturesque grounds of Parnham Park, allowing them to experience the natural beauty that inspired the novel's idyllic settings. Barton Cottage's modest charm provides a poignant contrast to the grandeur of Kingston Russell House, highlighting the class differences that were central to the novel's themes. By exploring these locations, fans of Jane Austen can gain a deeper appreciation for the world she created and the enduring appeal of her timeless classic. The picturesque grounds of Parnham Park offer a serene escape for those looking to immerse themselves in the Dorset countryside. Visitors can stroll through the beautifully manicured lawns and gardens, taking in the tranquil atmosphere that inspired the film's idyllic settings. In contrast, Kingston Russell House presents a stark visual difference with its baroque-style arched windows and white stone Georgian facade standing out amidst the lush greenery of Parnham Park. This stunning estate was used as the interior shots and main entrance for Norland Park in the film, providing an authentic glimpse into the lives of the wealthy Dashwood family. For those seeking a more immersive experience, it is possible to book a stay within the guest wing of Kingston Russell House, allowing visitors to fully indulge in the opulence and grandeur of the estate. Meanwhile, the production team transformed Ditsworthy Warren House, a dilapidated cottage nestled deep within Dartmoor National Park, into the modest and charming Barton Cottage. The stone structure required some renovation work before it could effectively capture the drama of the Dashwoods' new home, with windows and a new door being added to enhance its rustic charm. Despite these modifications, the stormy skies, rolling hills, and secluded surroundings of Dartmoor National Park still managed to evoke the sense of isolation and hardship that defined the Dashwoods' situation. Moody coastal scenery is a hallmark of any adaptation of Jane Austen's classic novel Sense and Sensibility. To capture this essence on film, the production team chose to shoot some key scenes at Mothecombe Beach in south Devon. This privately owned beach offers a tranquil atmosphere, with its soft sand and dramatic views of the surrounding coastline. A picturesque path leads down to the water's edge near the mouth of the Erme Estuary, providing visitors with a serene spot for contemplation. The beach is also home to a quaint teahouse where one can take refuge from the sea breeze. The tea room's proximity to the shore creates an idyllic setting, perfect for watching the waves roll in or simply enjoying a leisurely stroll along the shoreline. While fans of the novel may be searching for Marianne and Willoughby, they are unlikely to find them on this stretch of sand. Nevertheless, Mothecombe Beach's dramatic views make it easy to see why the production team chose this location for their adaptation of Sense and Sensibility. Barton Park, a key setting in the story, is actually a real-life 14th-century castle called Broughton Castle in Oxfordshire. The castle's imposing structure and beautiful gardens provide an ideal backdrop for the Dashwoods' humble abode. The castle's history dates back to the medieval era, with its fortified gatehouse and armor-adorned Great Hall reflecting its rich heritage. Today, visitors can cross the stone bridge over the moat and tour the historic rooms, gaining a glimpse into the lives of those who once called this place home. Despite being steeped in history, Broughton Castle has also played host to more modern productions, including The Crown and My Lady Jane. Its unique blend of medieval charm and elegant gardens makes it an attractive destination for travelers and fans of period dramas alike. Broughton Castle in Oxfordshire serves as the backdrop for Barton Park in the novel Sense and Sensibility. The castle's grandeur is a far cry from the humble abode that the Dashwood sisters are accustomed to. Its 14th-century architecture and fortified gatehouse make it seem more suited for medieval battles than hosting Regency-era dinner parties. In reality, Broughton Castle has been transformed into a tourist destination where visitors can explore its historic rooms and manicured gardens without the obligation of entertaining their landlord's relatives. The castle's stone bridge over the moat is a striking feature that adds to its charm. Travelers and fans of period dramas like The Crown and My Lady Jane, which also filmed at Broughton Castle, can now visit this historic estate. The Dashwood sisters' journey takes them to various locations in southern England as they navigate love, heartbreak, and social expectations. One of these locations is West Wycombe Park in Buckinghamshire, a stunning 18th-century Palladian villa that was built for Sir Francis Dashwood, a real-life member of the Dashwood family. West Wycombe Park's lavishly decorated staterooms, marble walls, and eclectic architectural style make it an intriguing destination. Visitors can explore the estate during the summer months when it opens to the public. The 45 acres of landscaped parkland surrounding the villa offer a serene atmosphere for hopeless romantics to stroll along the swan-shaped lake. The estate's beautiful gardens are a testament to the Dashwood family's love of nature and aesthetics. Today, West Wycombe Park is owned by the National Trust, which ensures its preservation for future generations to enjoy. The trust's efforts have made it possible for visitors to experience the beauty of this 18th-century villa. As the story unfolds, the Dashwood sisters face numerous challenges that test their sense and sensibility. Their journey takes them to various locations in southern England, each with its own unique charm and character. From the grandeur of Broughton Castle to the elegance of West Wycombe Park, these locations have been transformed into tourist destinations that showcase the beauty of English history. The legacy of Sense and Sensibility lives on through these locations, which continue to captivate audiences with their timeless themes and settings. As a testament to its enduring appeal, these locations remain popular among travelers and fans of period dramas alike, offering a glimpse into the world of Jane Austen's classic novel. articles.title: Multi-Mountain Ski Passes Gain Popularity Among Skiers and Snowboarders
articles.summary: Skiing and snowboarding enthusiasts are opting for multi-mountain passes as a cost-effective alternative to one-day lift tickets, which can exceed $300.
articles.content: Snow has already started falling in the Rocky Mountains and El Niño is expected to bring favorable weather conditions to certain US mountain regions, prompting skiers and snowboarders to start planning their winter getaways. Skiing and snowboarding are not typically budget-friendly activities, especially when considering additional expenses such as food, accommodations, and transportation on top of a single-day lift ticket that can cost upwards of $300 at some US resorts. The industry has shifted away from one-day lift tickets in favor of multi-mountain ski passes that offer significant discounts and perks like Epic's "Pay Over Time" option or Ikon's deals on friends and family tickets. Olivia Rowan, publisher of trade magazine Ski Area Management, points out that for those who hit the slopes more than six to eight days a season, multi-mountain passes have transformed the ski resort industry by expanding possibilities beyond their home mountain. To choose the right pass, skiers need to define their goals for the season, whether it's exploring new resorts or enjoying a day or two at each of several different mountains. When considering a ski pass for your winter travel plans, it's essential to weigh the costs against your skiing goals and preferences. The Epic Pass is an excellent option for individuals or families seeking unlimited access to some of the world's largest and most popular ski areas. The Vail-owned Epic Pass was the first multi-mountain pass in 2008 and has since become one of the industry's leading players, offering access to over 90 resorts across North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia. This extensive network includes top destinations like Park City, making it an ideal choice for those planning to spend a week at a more popular resort. For skiers who don't plan to hit the slopes during peak holiday weeks and weekends, the Epic Local Pass is a cost-effective alternative that excludes these dates at certain resorts. The standard Epic Pass costs $1,169 for unlimited access across all its resorts, while the customizable pass allows skiers to choose up to 7 days of skiing across different resort tiers. The Epic Pass also offers more budget-friendly options, including a basic plan that grants 7 days of skiing at 22 resorts in the Midwest, Northeast, and Mid-Atlantic for $337. This affordable choice is perfect for those who only need a shorter ski trip or prefer to split their time between multiple smaller resorts. The Epic Pass offers a wealth of options for travelers seeking diverse skiing experiences. One of its standout features is the range of destinations it covers, from bustling ski villages like Vail in Colorado to expansive terrain found at Les Trois Vallées in France. For those who crave deep snow, Rusutsu in Japan is an excellent choice. Another advantage of the Epic Pass is access to numerous smaller resorts near its major mountains, providing a chance for skiers and riders to explore uncrowded, under-the-radar options. In contrast to larger passes like Epic and Ikon, the Indy Pass focuses on partnering with smaller, independently owned resorts that often have deeply rooted local vibes. This season, the pass has introduced an upgrade allowing passholders to ski up to five days at 13 resorts, starting at $199. The Indy+ Pass, which doesn't come with blackout dates, costs $469 for adults and $299 for kids under 12. With sales often selling out quickly, it's essential to get on the waiting list now, although there's a chance that sales might reopen mid-season. Travelers can explore numerous options with the Indy Pass, such as Jay Peak in Vermont for East Coast snow, White Pass in Washington for family-friendly skiing, and Black Mountain in New Hampshire for an excellent aprés experience. The Ikon Pass offers an extensive range of options for winter travelers, granting access to over 70 resorts across 13 countries. Some notable destinations within the US include Jackson Hole, Deer Valley, and Aspen Snowmass. Pricing varies depending on individual needs, with tiered passes available. The unlimited pass starts at $1,529 for adults, while young adults aged 13-22 can opt for a more affordable option starting at $1,129. Children between 5-12 years old can purchase the unlimited pass for $499. In addition to the unlimited and base passes, Ikon also offers personalized options for those who may not be able to get out as much during the season. This includes two, three, or four-day passes at participating resorts. Resorts such as Big Bear Mountain in California are ideal for beginners, offering a more relaxed learning environment. Meanwhile, Deer Valley in Utah boasts exciting new terrain and amenities that cater to those seeking a thrilling experience. The Snow Pass offers two days of skiing at each partner resort, but its selection is currently limited to 14 locations, mostly in the Northeast region. A notable aspect of the Snow Pass is that additional days can be purchased at a discounted rate of 30% off the retail price, providing flexibility for travelers with varying ski schedules. The Snow Pass also offers an alternative option called Snow Triple Play, which grants three days of skiing across its network of 23 partner resorts. Resort options within easy reach from New York City include Mountain Creek in New Jersey and Cranmore in New Hampshire, both of which cater to families. The cost of a Mountain Collective Pass varies depending on age and residency status, with adult passes priced at $729, teen passes at $594, and junior passes for those 6-12 years old costing $304. Skiers can supplement their pass by purchasing day tickets to specific resorts at half off the regular price, offering flexibility for those who want to explore more terrain than their initial allocation allows. Jackson Hole in Wyoming is particularly well-suited for thrill-seekers with its steep slopes, while Revelstoke in British Columbia offers consistent deep snow conditions. articles.title: New Year Travel Plans Revealed for Well-Traveled Women
articles.summary: Well-traveled women from diverse backgrounds are already looking ahead, sharing their aspirations for the upcoming year, with destinations including Antarctica and Lapland.
articles.content: As the calendar flips to 2027, a new year of travel possibilities beckons for many. However, turning bucket list dreams into reality can be a daunting task, especially when faced with limited vacation days and financial constraints. Well-traveled women from diverse backgrounds are already looking ahead, sharing their aspirations for the upcoming year. From photographers to artisans, interior designers to rock climbers, each has unique travel plans that reflect their passions and interests. Pier Nirandara, a travel writer and underwater photographer, is one such individual with big plans. She's been fascinated by the polar regions since childhood, growing up in Bangkok's tropical climate. Her dream of diving in Antarctica has finally taken shape, as she prepares to join Aurora Expeditions, a pioneer in polar diving, next year. For Nirandara, experiencing Antarctica underwater will be an entirely new and thrilling adventure. Having visited the White Continent before, she's eager to witness its breathtaking beauty from a different perspective, surrounded by icebergs, seals, and penguins. Next up is Stargazing in Lapland, another destination that has long been on one traveler's radar. Lapland is high on one traveler's list of destinations for 2027, with plans to visit in February when direct flights from Milan to Rovaniemi, Finland become available. The itinerary includes two nights in Rovaniemi and two in Levi, allowing ample time to explore the region's winter wonderland. A highlight of the trip is a stay in glass cabins that offer breathtaking views of the northern lights and starry skies. The experience promises to be both exhilarating and relaxing, with opportunities to engage in activities such as visiting a reindeer farm, husky sledding, and snowshoe hikes through frost-covered pine forests. Alternatively, guests can unwind by a crackling fire, wrapped in a warm blanket, surrounded by the serene beauty of the winter landscape. The region's natural scenery is not the only draw; travelers will also have access to unique cultural experiences that showcase the traditions of the indigenous Sami people. In addition to Lapland, another destination on one traveler's radar for 2027 is Morocco. A riad stay in Marrakech is being eyed as a prime opportunity to immerse oneself in the country's vibrant culture and rich history. The Peloponnese Peninsula in Greece has caught the attention of professional climber Sasha DiGiulian. While many flock to Greece for its idyllic beaches and Mediterranean charm, DiGiulian's curiosity led her to explore the central region of Arcadia. DiGiulian is drawn to the fertile valleys of Arcadia, known for their strong culinary and agricultural traditions. The region produces a diverse array of products, including apples, sour cherries, eggplants, cheeses from mountain sheep and goats, walnuts, chestnuts, and wild mushrooms. This bounty has made her focus on a specific hotel in the area. Manna, located on Mount Mainalo among hiking trails and dense forests, has piqued DiGiulian's interest. The mountain is home to high-altitude honey cultivated from fir trees, a unique product that adds to the region's rich culinary heritage. This distinctive honey production process has made Manna an attractive destination for those seeking a genuine taste of Arcadia. For Noreen Wasti, cook and author, 2027 promises new adventures in South America and a return to her family's homeland of Mauritius. A first-time visitor to the continent, Wasti is eager to explore Peru and marvel at Machu Picchu. She envisions guided tours through the Sacred Valley and plenty of time for exploration. Wasti also looks forward to revisiting Mauritius with fresh eyes as a tourist this time around. She longs for the island's hospitality and the opportunity to indulge in local cuisine, which she misses dearly when away. Nashmita Rajiah's travels typically revolve around family obligations and catching up with loved ones. Her desire for cultural immersion is evident in her work as an interior designer, where she continuously scouts destinations for In Hand's newsletter and group trips by exploring regions rich in traditional craft through the lens of local artisans. A forthcoming trip to Morocco's Atlas Mountains will allow Rajiah to visit female Amazigh weavers in their homes and learn about the intricate process of weaving Berber rugs at its source, rather than just buying them at a store. This hands-on approach allows her to delve deeper into the culture and traditions surrounding this craft, which has been passed down through generations. The trip will be based in Imlil, a small mountain town with strong roots in real Amazigh village life, where Rajiah will stay at Kasbah du Toubkal. It's an experience she's longed for years to have. Rajiah is perpetually on the lookout for new destinations and experiences to share with her audience through In Hand. Favignana Island in Sicily's Egadi Islands is a destination on many travelers' radars for 2027. The island offers an idyllic setting with crystal-clear waters, numerous secluded coves, and a bike-friendly terrain that allows visitors to easily explore its entire circumference. The local cuisine remains a major draw, with tuna remaining the star of the show despite the closure of the old canning factory. A highlight for many will be indulging in traditional dishes such as spaghetti with bottarga, a delicacy made from cured grey mullet roe. For those seeking an immersive experience, Villa Zu Nillu is a prime choice. Perched above its own ancient Roman quarry, this property boasts breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape and features an inviting pool and lush Mediterranean garden. Visitors can unwind amidst the tranquil surroundings, replete with historic charm. Photographer Andrea Gentl plans to escape the heat by heading north to Finland in 2027. With a focus on experiencing the country's midnight sun, he will be joined by his decorative arts friend and her family for a lakeside adventure. They aim to visit notable design destinations such as Helsinki's Aalto House and the Hvitträsk museum. The itinerary includes renting a mökki, a traditional Finnish lakeside cabin, where they can unwind with activities like swimming, hiking, and exploring the nearby archipelagos. However, Gentl admits he may regret his decision if the midnight sun proves too overwhelming for his young companions to sleep through. The Terre di Sacra Estate in Italy is among the destinations that Philomena Schurer Merckoll, founder of Riad Mena and hospitality group Egypt Beyond Weaving, hopes to visit in 2027. She is considering either glamping on the beach or staying in one of their villas. Akosua Afriyie-Kumi, founder of AAKS, has a fascination with Japan that stems from her work as a designer using raffia and traditional weaving techniques. She finds it intriguing that Japanese culture values craftsmanship and handmade objects, which she would like to learn more about by visiting Kyoto's historic temples and meeting local artisans. articles.title: Maldon Salt Investigation Finds Use of German-Mined Rock Salt
articles.summary: Recent investigations have raised questions about the authenticity of Maldon Salt's production process.
articles.content: Maldon Salt's reputation is built on its unique production process in Essex, where pyramid-shaped flakes are made using water from the Blackwater Estuary. However, recent investigations have raised questions about the company's authenticity. A probe found that German-mined rock salt is also used in Maldon's production process, sparking concerns about the label's accuracy. The term "100% sea salt flakes on Maldon's labels has left some shoppers wondering what it really means. Does it imply that the salt comes entirely from the sea, or can other sources be used? The distinction is crucial for consumers who value the product's origins and manufacturing process. Maldon claims to use a traditional method called salt-on-salt, where rock salt is added to seawater to create brine, which is then heated and evaporated. According to the company, this process produces the same distinctive taste and texture that cooks have come to expect from Maldon Salt. The rock salt used in this method is described as ancient sea salt. Regulators investigated Maldon's production process between 2019 and 2020 but took no further action. Officials explained that there was no specific law defining what constitutes sea salt. While the findings do not raise concerns about food safety, they do highlight the need for greater transparency in labeling. Residents have documented deliveries of German rock salt to Maldon's Essex site, raising questions about the accuracy of the company's labeling and manufacturing process. The investigation has sparked a wider debate about how much detail consumers should be given about a product's origins and production methods. The controversy surrounding Maldon Salt has led to questions about transparency in labeling and marketing. From a nutritional standpoint, both sea salt and rock salt are essentially sodium chloride, making it unlikely that adding German rock salt would significantly alter the product's overall nutritional profile, according to registered dietitian Stefani Sassos. Specialty salts like Maldon's may differ in flavor, texture, crystal size, and mineral composition compared to table salt or other types of specialty salts, but these differences do not provide any substantial health benefits, Sassos points out. The label on Maldon's U.S. product page lists the ingredient as sea salt flakes and describes it as hand-harvested in Maldon, Essex, which may lead some consumers to assume that they are getting a truly authentic product. Consumers should be able to trust that what they're paying for is exactly what they get, Sassos emphasizes, suggesting that if imported rock salt is being added, this information should be clearly disclosed and transparently communicated. The labeling discrepancy between Canadian and US versions of Maldon salt is more than just a semantic difference. According to regulatory guidelines, salt from a mine cannot be labeled as sea salt in Canada. On packaging, this distinction manifests as different ingredient descriptions: salt flakes on the Canadian tub versus sea salt flakes on the US version. This variation may seem minor, but it highlights how shoppers in different markets are presented with distinct information about product ingredients. The rules governing labeling requirements vary between countries, and the Canadian Food Inspection Agency's stance is clear: mine-sourced salt should not be marketed as sea salt. However, this rule does not dictate US labeling standards, resulting in differing descriptions on Maldon products sold across international borders. Maldon's manufacturing process might not impact how consumers use their product at home. Nevertheless, for those who prioritize the origin of ingredients, additional details about production methods can help them assess whether the label accurately reflects their expectations. Additional details about production methods can be crucial for shoppers seeking to understand the authenticity of products claiming artisanal" or "hand-harvested" origins. When scrutinizing product labels, it's essential to consider whether the manufacturer is transparent about its methods and suppliers, even if it doesn't meet the traditional definition of artisanal. articles.title: US All-Inclusive Resorts Offer Variety Beyond Tropical Destinations
articles.summary: US-based all-inclusive resorts offer packages that cover food, drinks, and activities in various guises, including dude ranches and wellness-focused retreats.
articles.content: The all-inclusive resort concept has long been associated with tropical destinations in Mexico and the Caribbean, but a closer look at the US reveals a wealth of options that cater to diverse tastes and preferences. From the sun-kissed beaches of Florida to the rugged coastline of California, an increasing number of resorts are offering packages that cover food, drinks, and activities, often without breaking the bank. Contrary to expectations, these domestic all-inclusive resorts come in various guises, including dude ranches serving elevated Western cuisine and wellness-focused retreats nestled in desert landscapes. A key distinction between US-based all-inclusive resorts and their international counterparts lies in the fine print, it's essential to read carefully about what's included in your rate, as some properties may not cover alcohol or certain activities. To get the most out of these packages, it's crucial to understand what's covered and what's extra, including activities like horseback riding or fly-fishing that might incur additional costs. When researching US all-inclusive resorts, be aware that some properties, particularly dude ranches and wellness retreats, may have specific requirements, such as minimum stay periods or select check-in days. This means being flexible with your travel dates can help you make the most of these unique experiences, which often offer a chance to unwind in tranquil surroundings. Castle Hot Springs in Morristown, Arizona, is one such luxury desert oasis that's been around since the 1800s, its natural hot springs are a major draw, with temperatures ranging from 86 to 106 degrees Fahrenheit. Guests can indulge in meals made from ingredients grown on-site, but note that alcoholic drinks aren't included in the rate. Castle Hot Springs in Arizona offers luxurious accommodations at a rate that starts at $1,250 per night for double occupancy. The resort has specific requirements for its guests, including a two- or three-night minimum stay for most dates due to its limited availability during peak periods. However, there are some exceptions to this rule, with the resort closed for most of July and August every year. Meanwhile, in California, Alila Ventana Big Sur is another top destination that has been winning over travelers and industry experts alike since its conversion into an all-inclusive property in 2020. This stylish retreat boasts a range of accommodation options, including 54 rooms and suites that exude rustic-chic charm while offering luxurious amenities like walk-in showers, soaking tubs, and stocked minibars. Guests can choose from various room types to suit their preferences, such as those with private decks or fireplaces for added coziness. The resort's modern American restaurant, The Sur House, takes pride in serving dishes made from produce grown on-site and locally sourced ingredients, although it's worth noting that alcoholic drinks are not included in the all-inclusive package. Beyond dining, visitors can enjoy a range of activities like hiking, practicing yoga, or relaxing in the Japanese hot baths for some much-needed rejuvenation. The culinary experience at this resort is redefining American cuisine, thanks to its signature "Foothills Cuisine concept. Meals are carefully prepared using seasonal ingredients foraged from a 4-acre on-site garden and other locally sourced ingredients, ensuring every bite is fresh and flavorful. Accommodations range from three- to five-bedroom houses with ample space to spread out to more intimate 1,080-square-foot Hill Cottages, each equipped with private golf carts and warm fireplaces. The resort's Historic Rooms are smaller but no less charming, featuring antique decor that exudes classic elegance. In addition to its culinary offerings, the resort boasts an impressive array of activities, including hiking, yoga, horseback riding, and fly-fishing. Other pursuits include top-tier concerts, spa treatments, and special programs designed for children's entertainment and education. articles.title: Measles outbreaks in the US linked to declining vaccination rates
articles.summary: Experts warn that congenital measles is a public health issue due to rising cases among newborns whose mothers contracted the virus during pregnancy.
articles.content: Measles outbreaks in the US are taking a disturbing turn as doctors report a surge in newborns born with the disease. The alarming trend has experts sounding the alarm about congenital measles, which occurs when a pregnant woman passes the virus to her unborn child. The condition can have devastating consequences for babies, leading to serious complications or even death. According to preliminary figures from a medical journal, 13 cases of congenital measles were reported in the US between January and September this year during large measles outbreaks. The emergence of congenital measles is linked to declining vaccination rates, which have allowed the virus to spread rapidly across the country. As a result, the Pan American Health Organization is expected to announce that the US has lost its measles-free status, a distinction it had maintained since 2000. Experts are warning that this trend is not just a concern for individual families but also a public health issue, as the virus continues to spread with alarming frequency. According to the CDC, there have been over 7,500 measles cases in the past two years alone, fueling fears of further outbreaks and complications. The alarming trend of measles cases in the US is having far-reaching consequences, particularly for newborns whose mothers contracted the virus during pregnancy. According to a public health alert published by NEJM Evidence, there were 112 confirmed cases of measles during pregnancy in the past two years alone, with nearly all of these cases occurring among women who had not been vaccinated against measles or whose vaccination status was unknown. Getting vaccinated before pregnancy and maintaining high vaccination rates in communities are crucial steps to prevent measles and related complications, as emphasized by CDC scientists who authored the alert. This is a stark reminder that even with widespread vaccination efforts, there is still a significant risk of congenital measles if mothers are not protected. The American Academy of Pediatrics has been working closely with healthcare providers to raise awareness about congenital measles, which can have devastating consequences for newborns. In fact, Pennsylvania's health department recently published an advisory for healthcare providers, schools, childcare centers, and others in the state, where the largest measles outbreak is currently underway. As a result of declining vaccination rates, we are now seeing levels of measles that haven't been seen in 30 years, according to Dr. Adam Ratner, a member of the American Academy of Pediatrics' infectious diseases committee. This has led to an increase in congenital measles cases, a condition that was once extremely rare due to high vaccination rates. The rise in unvaccinated women of childbearing age has created a vulnerable population susceptible to measles. As these women become pregnant, they are at risk of contracting the disease, which can have devastating consequences for both mother and baby. To prevent this, doctors recommend that women receive the MMR vaccine before pregnancy, ensuring their bodies produce antibodies that protect not only themselves but also their unborn child through the placenta. This protection can last several months after birth, providing a crucial safeguard against measles complications, but it's essential to note that the MMR vaccine cannot be administered during pregnancy itself. If an unvaccinated woman is exposed to measles while pregnant and hasn't developed immunity, she can receive a solution containing antibodies within six days to reduce the risk of infection. The alarming trend of babies born with measles has sparked concerns among medical professionals. Measles-related complications can be severe in newborns, and doctors are particularly worried about the risk of Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE). According to experts, children who contract measles at birth may develop SSPE sooner than their peers who get infected later on. This worrying trend is only just beginning to come to light. The decline in vaccination rates across the US has raised fears that outbreaks could become more frequent and severe. While a 95% measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination rate is considered sufficient to prevent widespread outbreaks, many communities have fallen below this threshold. Nationally, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported that only 92.4% of US kindergarteners received their required MMR shots in the 2025-26 academic year. The vulnerable population of infants too young to be vaccinated is at risk due to low vaccination rates among adults. Since the first MMR dose is administered between 12 to 15 months old, babies under this age are not protected against measles. In areas where outbreaks have been reported, the earliest a baby can receive their shots is six months old. Concerns are being raised by doctors about US babies born with measles, as vaccination rates continue to be a pressing issue. Babies born in areas where outbreaks have been reported may not receive their shots until six months old, leaving them vulnerable to the highly contagious disease. This delayed immunization schedule can put infants at risk of contracting and spreading measles, despite efforts by public health officials to contain outbreaks. articles.title: Cruise Lines Offer More Options for Solo Travelers
articles.summary: Cruise lines are often designed to cater to couples and families, but a growing number of solo travelers are taking advantage of new options available on ships around the world.
articles.content: Cruise lines are often designed to cater to couples and families, but a growing number of solo travelers are taking advantage of new options available on ships around the world. Most cruise cabins are set up for two people, which means that advertised rates are based on double occupancy - unless you're traveling with someone who's willing to pay an extra fare. This premium can be as high as 100%, making it a costly option for solo travelers. However, there is some good news: several cruise lines have started adding cabins specifically designed for solo travelers, and these often come with lower single supplement charges. Some lines also offer promotions that reduce or waive these fees entirely. A key factor in choosing the right cruise line as a solo traveler isn't just about getting a good price - it's also about meeting other like-minded individuals through organized events and activities. Some cruise lines excel at creating welcoming environments for solo travelers, while others fall short. In response to growing demand from solo cruisers, a number of major cruise lines have expanded their offerings in recent years. One notable pioneer is Norwegian Cruise Line, which introduced an entire zone of small "studio cabins on its then-new ship, Norwegian Epic, back in 2010. These new options give solo travelers more choices and flexibility when planning their trip. By considering factors such as price, cabin options, and onboard amenities, it's possible to find a cruise line that meets your needs and budget. In the next part of this article, we'll take a closer look at six top picks for cruise lines that are particularly well-suited to solo travelers - from Norwegian Cruise Line's innovative studio" cabins to other lines that offer guaranteed single occupancy rates or organized events for solo cruisers. Norwegian Cruise Line's innovative solo cabin concept has been a resounding success, prompting other cruise lines to follow suit and cater to this growing demographic. These compact but stylish cabins are designed to maximize storage space, providing solo travelers with a comfortable and efficient place to rest their heads while at sea. The Norwegian Epic boasts an exclusive Studio Lounge where solo travelers can mingle with like-minded individuals during daily hosted happy hour gatherings in the lounge's bar and television area. Norwegian has expanded its solo cabin offerings to eight more ships, including its three newest vessels: Norwegian Aqua, Norwegian Viva, and Norwegian Prima. Each of these newer ships features a dedicated solo complex, with Norwegian Aqua boasting an impressive 93-cabin spread across two decks, while the smaller Norwegian Viva and Prima offer 73 cabins each. In addition to these larger complexes, other Norwegian ships also cater to solo travelers, including the bigger Norwegian Encore, Escape, and Bliss, which all feature an 82-cabin solo complex. Two older ships in the fleet, the Norwegian Breakaway and Getaway, have been adapted with smaller solo areas featuring 59 cabins each. Norwegian's Hawaii-based Pride of America offers a more limited but still convenient option for solo travelers, with four dedicated solo cabins available. Norwegian's solo digs often have ocean views, but many of these cabins are actually studio rooms with balconies, offering a more expansive space for solo travelers to relax and take in the surroundings. Royal Caribbean's Anthem of the Seas boasts an impressive array of solo-friendly features, including several studio ocean-view cabins that cater specifically to the needs of single travelers on the go. In addition to its newer ships like Anthem of the Seas, Royal Caribbean also offers solo accommodations on some of its larger Oasis Class vessels, such as Symphony of the Seas and Wonder of the Seas, providing ample opportunities for solo cruisers to explore new horizons. While it's true that not all Royal Caribbean ships have an abundance of solo cabins, several of its Voyager Class and Radiance Class vessels also offer dedicated single rooms, albeit in smaller numbers, often just two or three per ship. To connect with fellow travelers, Royal Caribbean has introduced a range of meetups specifically for solo cruisers on board its ships, providing a platform to forge new friendships and shared experiences while at sea. In contrast to the virtual verandas found on some other cruise lines, Royal Caribbean's solo cabins offer genuine ocean views through large picture windows, allowing guests to connect with nature in real-time without relying on digital projections. Cunard Lines has carved out a niche for itself as a premium option for solo travelers seeking an old-world charm and elegance during their voyage, with dedicated single staterooms available on three of its ships: Queen Mary 2, Queen Elizabeth, and Queen Victoria. The amenities for solo travelers on Cunard Lines' ships are designed to make them feel right at home. Dining options in the Britannia Restaurant cater to those who prefer to eat alone, while also offering the chance to join other passengers for a meal. In addition to this flexibility, solo travelers can enjoy luxury perks such as complimentary breakfast in bed and Penhaligon's toiletries. These touches are meant to make their stay on board feel truly special. Cunard Lines has made significant efforts to create a welcoming environment for its solo passengers. The line hosts social events like coffee mornings and cocktail receptions specifically for solo travelers, providing opportunities to meet new people. On select voyages, Cunard also brings aboard dance hosts who partner with passengers at evening balls, adding an extra layer of fun and excitement. These events are reminiscent of a bygone era, but they're still a great way to meet fellow travelers and make lasting connections. Silversea Cruises offers a unique approach to catering to solo travelers. Unlike some other lines, Silversea doesn't have specific cabin categories for solo passengers, instead offering single supplements that range from 10% to 25% on select sailings. Occasionally, the line even waives these supplements entirely during short-term promotions. Virgin Voyages has designed its ships to cater specifically to solo travelers, offering a unique experience that sets them apart from other cruise lines. Each of Virgin's four vessels - Scarlet Lady, Valiant Lady, Resilient Lady, and Brilliant Lady - features 46 cabins tailored for lone travelers, accounting for nearly one-third of the ship's total capacity. These ships have only around 1,330 cabins in total, making the number of solo-friendly rooms a significant proportion of the overall capacity. The solo accommodations on Virgin Voyages' ships include two types of rooms: the windowless Solo Insider and the Solo Sea View cabin with windows. Solo Sea View cabins measure approximately 130 square feet and offer stunning views from their forward-facing locations at the front of the ship. However, seasoned cruisers know that cabins in this location can be more prone to motion sickness during rough seas, a consideration for solo travelers who may not have a partner to provide support. When it comes to meeting fellow travelers, smaller ships are often more conducive to socializing than their larger counterparts. This is because passengers tend to interact with each other repeatedly on tours, in lounges and by the pool. As a result, solo cruisers can increase their chances of striking up conversations and forming lasting connections. Smaller ships also offer a higher likelihood of meeting other single travelers, as lines operating these vessels often provide discounts for solo cruisers. This is reflected in the higher percentage of individual passengers on board, making it easier to find like-minded individuals. For those who prefer the intimacy of river cruising, there are several options available that cater specifically to solo travelers. Some river cruise lines waive or significantly lower single supplement charges, providing a more affordable and inclusive experience for those traveling alone. Avalon Waterways is one such line that offers a range of benefits for solo cruisers. On select departures in Europe, the company waives its single supplement charge for certain cabins. Additionally, AmaWaterways charges just 25% above the standard rate for solo travelers booking nonsuite cabins. Some river cruise lines also offer dedicated solo cabins with no additional supplement fees. For example, AmaWaterways has four ships in Europe that feature two such cabins. This unique offering allows solo travelers to enjoy a more affordable and convenient experience without sacrificing comfort or amenities. Ultimately, smaller ships and specialized river cruise lines are ideal choices for solo travelers looking to connect with like-minded individuals while exploring new destinations. By opting for these options, solo cruisers can increase their chances of forming meaningful connections and creating lasting memories on the high seas. He believes that their experience and expertise will enable them to prioritize what matters most at any given time. The immediate priority for Pochettino and his team is the game against Haiti tomorrow in Cincinnati. articles.title: Jury Decision-Making Process Analyzed Through Virtual Mock Juries
articles.summary: A new study is shedding light on how juries make decisions, particularly when faced with disagreement among its members.
articles.content: A new study is shedding light on how juries make decisions, particularly when faced with disagreement among its members. Researchers led by Tova Cohen, a Ph.D. student at Rutgers School of Criminal Justice, conducted an in-depth analysis of virtual mock juries to gain insight into the decision-making process. The study involved 35 participants who were divided into seven virtual mock juries, allowing researchers to examine individual characteristics and group dynamics. The researchers aimed to understand how jurors interact with each other during deliberations, especially when faced with conflicting opinions. This is crucial for collective legal decision-making in the U.S. criminal legal system. Cohen emphasizes that understanding jury deliberation is essential for grasping the complexities of the process. "Jury deliberation is a significant component of the U.S. criminal legal system and is important for collective legal decision-making," she said. By examining how jurors respond to disagreement, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of the factors influencing their decisions. The study's findings reveal that personal characteristics play a role in determining individual participation levels during deliberations. However, other traits such as agreeableness, openness, and civic engagement were not found to be predictive of increased involvement in discussions. Researchers also discovered that disagreement among jurors can serve as an opportunity for individuals to express competing interpretations of the evidence. After one deliberation, participants' initial verdict preferences shifted, with some who initially voted "not guilty" ultimately reporting a guilty verdict. The study's results suggest that understanding jury decisions requires more than just examining final verdicts. articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys fell to the San Francisco 49ers despite Dak Prescott's impressive performance, as their porous defense continues to plague the team.
articles.content: The Dallas Cowboys' struggles continue as quarterback Dak Prescott threw for five touchdown passes in their recent 46-40 loss to San Francisco, but it was not enough to overcome another porous defense. Prescott's impressive performance tied his career high for touchdowns thrown in a single game, yet the team's inability to stop their opponents remains a major concern. The Cowboys are now working on a third consecutive season without a postseason appearance, despite having an 11th-year quarterback with a significant annual salary of $60 million. The team's defense has been a liability all year round, failing to make crucial stops and allowing big plays that ultimately cost them games. Prescott acknowledged the team's scoring capabilities but emphasized the need for their defense to step up its game. Despite occasional flashes of brilliance, the Cowboys' defense continues to struggle with consistency, leaving their offense to pick up the slack. The lack of a reliable defensive unit has put immense pressure on Prescott and his teammates to perform at an exceptionally high level every time they take the field. Prescott's comments after the game highlighted the team's awareness of their problems, but it remains to be seen whether they can address these issues before it's too late. The Cowboys' porous defense continues to plague the team as they prepare to face Tennessee on Sunday. Dallas's inability to contain Christian McCaffrey was a major concern last week, as he became the first running back in NFL history to record two touchdown catches of at least 65 yards in the same game. His 74-yard and 66-yard receptions were significant blows to the Cowboys' defense. The team struggled to keep up with McCaffrey's speed and agility. The defense also allowed Deebo Samuel to run 70 yards for a touchdown on a reverse play, which added to their woes. Furthermore, running back Kaelon Black managed to push aside defenders and score a 25-yard touchdown run. The Cowboys' inability to contain opponents' big plays is becoming a recurring theme. Dallas has now given up at least one touchdown of 50-plus yards in three consecutive games, setting an unfortunate franchise record for most yards allowed at home (584). This season alone, the team has surrendered nine plays of at least 50 yards, more than double the number of any other NFL team. Coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed his frustration with the defense's performance after the game, using strong words to describe their shortcomings. When asked about his confidence in Christian Parker, a first-time defensive coordinator, Schottenheimer acknowledged that there are issues to be addressed. George Pickens' impressive performance on Sunday was a bright spot for the Cowboys, but it wasn't enough to overcome their struggling defense. The young receiver set career highs in targets (18), catches (11) and yards (145) with three touchdown catches, yet his team's inability to capitalize on his success remains a concern. The Cowboys' porous defense has been a persistent problem for Schottenheimer, who is now in his second season at the helm. The team's struggles on this side of the ball have become so pronounced that it's difficult to describe just how bad they've been. One possible explanation for their woes could be the aftermath of the Micah Parsons trade. Despite Prescott's valiant efforts to keep the game close, he ultimately fell short in leading his team to victory. His 30 completions out of 51 attempts were a testament to his determination, but it's worth noting that this level of passing has been a recipe for disaster for the Cowboys in the past. In fact, they've lost seven times when Prescott exceeds the 50-attempt mark. The atmosphere at AT & T Stadium on Sunday was unlike anything experienced by fans in over a decade. The strong presence of visiting supporters created an unusual home-game feel, with many fans clad in opposing colors dominating the stands. This sea of red was a striking sight, one that left some scratching their heads about what it means to be "America's Team" in today's NFL. The Cowboys' struggles on both sides of the ball have become increasingly frustrating for fans and coaches alike. As they continue to search for answers, one thing is clear: their defense needs significant improvement if they hope to compete with the league's top teams. The Cowboys' high-powered offense has been unable to compensate for their porous defense this season, a trend that continued in their latest game. Coach Schottenheimer pointed out that ankle injuries to key players Tyler Booker and DaRon Bland were major concerns following the match. A look at franchise history reveals that the Cowboys have experienced similar struggles before, having lost three games where they scored 40 or more points. articles.summary: Celebrities gathered at the Ray Dolby Ballroom in Ovation Hollywood for the Governors Awards ceremony.
articles.content: The Governors Awards ceremony kicked off on a star-studded night at the Ray Dolby Ballroom in Ovation Hollywood. The event, hosted by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, honored outstanding achievements in the film industry. Celebrities began arriving at the venue around 5 pm, with Nathan Fielder being one of the first to arrive. He caught up with fellow guests about his outfit for the evening - a midnight-blue Armani tuxedo that turned heads. Parker Posey made her grand entrance soon after, flashing a radiant smile in a stunning black lace-and-mesh ensemble. She was accompanied by Martin McDonagh and Sarah Finn, with whom she had recently collaborated on the comedy-thriller Wild Horse Nine. The evening's festivities were accompanied by a reception outside the ballroom, where guests mingled over trays of savory bites, including mini burgers and pierogies. Servers expertly navigated through the crowded room, offering an assortment of appetizers to keep attendees satisfied. One notable interaction caught the attention of onlookers: Glenn Close politely declined an offered appetizer, but her kind gesture brightened the server's day. The staff member couldn't help but smile at the brief exchange. As guests began making their way into the ballroom, an announcement over the loudspeaker signaled the start of dinner service. Charles Melton lingered a little longer outside, chatting with actress Piper Curda and other attendees. Meanwhile, Emmy Rossum arrived just as the five-minute warning was announced, squeezing past Elizabeth Debicki and Carla Gugino, who were engrossed in conversation. Attendees were treated to a variety of appetizers as they took their seats at the Governors Awards. The selection included smoked salmon oscar matzah, which was likely a nod to the classic Oscars ceremony. Fennel-crusted seared tuna on confit potato and spicy carrot hummus on pumpernickel were also among the options. A wagyu carpaccio roll with winter vegetables rounded out the assortment. Lynette Howell Taylor, president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, was the first to address the room. Her remarks kicked off a celebratory evening honoring five artists for their outstanding contributions to film. Taylor's words sparked a round of applause from the audience, setting a positive tone for the rest of the ceremony. When it comes to recognizing exceptional careers, Howell Taylor noted that there is often more to the story than meets the eye. "Take a look at the five artists we're honoring here tonight," she began, emphasizing the importance of considering the years of determination and perseverance behind their achievements. The audience was receptive to her message, responding with applause. The years of hard work and dedication that contribute to an artist's success are often overlooked in favor of their iconic performances and groundbreaking achievements. Howell Taylor highlighted this point, acknowledging that the path to greatness is rarely straightforward. "When we think about their extraordinary careers, it's easy to see the great films," she said, but added that there is more to consider. Determination and perseverance are essential qualities for any artist seeking to make a lasting impact in their field. Howell Taylor emphasized this point, encouraging the audience to look beyond the surface-level accomplishments of the honorees. "What we don't always see are the years of determination behind them," she said, underscoring the importance of recognizing these qualities. Following her remarks, dinner was served, with guests enjoying a pan-roasted chicken dish accompanied by truffle velouté and roasted heirloom carrots. The meal was rounded out by a side of potato purée. The evening's selection of wines included La Clarté de Haut-Brion, Le Dragon de Quintus, and Piper-Heidsieck Champagne. The first honoree of the evening was Norman, who received an honorary award presented by Mahershala Ali. "I am so deeply honored to present the first award tonight to a pioneering animator, story artist, and writer," Ali said, highlighting Norman's impressive 70-year career in film. The atmosphere in the room shifted dramatically as Close took the stage, her emotions palpable on her face. A mixture of laughter and applause erupted when she stumbled over her words while reading from the teleprompter, momentarily breaking the tension. Close's speech was a candid look back at her past, revealing that she had been part of a restrictive cult from age seven to 22. The rules she was forced to follow were starkly illustrated by her recollection of being told not to look in mirrors or engage in flirtation. Instead, she was instructed on how to dress and speak. The actress's comments served as a poignant reminder of the challenges she had overcome before finding success in the entertainment industry. It was clear that Close's experiences had shaped her perspective and informed her work. Matt Damon took to the stage next, playfully poking fun at Ridley Scott who accepted his award remotely. The actor's joke about being "totally available for certain films directed by Scott drew laughter from the room, a welcome respite from the more serious moments of the evening. Damon's lighthearted remark was a testament to the camaraderie and good humor that pervaded the event. His willingness to poke fun at himself added to the convivial atmosphere, making his appearance all the more enjoyable. The ceremony also honored Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award, presented by Julianne Moore and Todd Haynes. Before accepting their award, however, the duo had a surprise in store for the audience: a performance by Neil Patrick Harris singing The Origin of Love" from Hedwig and the Angry Inch, a film produced by Vachon and Koffler. The ceremony's closing moments were filled with a sense of nostalgia as Pam Koffler looked back on her decades-long collaboration with her partner. She reflected on their long-standing partnership, which has spanned over 30 years and produced numerous films through their production company Killer Films. Koffler's recollection of their early days working together was marked by a sense of determination to establish themselves in the industry. Their decision to name their company Killer Films was a deliberate choice that reflected their ambition to produce high-quality content. The evening's events seemed to hint at an exciting awards season ahead, with Hollywood already gearing up for a memorable celebration. articles.title: Gérard Darel Jeans Popular among Parisians at Fashion Week
articles.summary: The Anna jeans from Gérard Darel were seen repeatedly on showgoers and locals during Paris Fashion Week last month, showcasing the brand's understated yet elegant style.
articles.content: Fashion Week in Paris last month was abuzz with style trends, but one particular trend caught my attention - the ubiquity of a specific type of jeans among showgoers and locals alike. The flashiest outfits on display were often courtesy of brands sponsoring the events, making it difficult to report on street style without feeling like I was promoting a product rather than observing authentic fashion choices. In contrast, Parisians seemed uninterested in following trends or dressing for effect. They preferred to stick with what worked for them, and one item that kept popping up was jeans - not just any jeans, but a particular high-waisted, flared style that I saw repeatedly during my time at the shows. As I watched a woman climb onto her Lime bike outside Le Saint-Gervais bar, I found myself drawn to her outfit. She caught my eye and paused for a moment before swinging her leg over the saddle, giving me just enough time to ask where she got her jeans from. "Anna," she said finally, "Gérard Darel." The brand has been synonymous with effortless French style for decades, its discreet designs effortlessly blending into everyday Parisian life. Gérard Darel's iconic 24H bag is a ubiquitous sight on the city's Métro, often stuffed with school supplies and tangled headphones during the morning rush. This understated approach to fashion is a hallmark of the brand's aesthetic, one that has been adopted by generations of French women who value simplicity and elegance in their wardrobes. As for the jeans themselves, they may have originated in America but have since become an integral part of the Gérard Darel wardrobe, with a timeless design that never goes out of style. The Anna jeans, designed by former creative director Valérie Gerbi, are a particular favorite among fashion enthusiasts and celebrities alike, including supermodel Kate Moss who has been spotted wearing them on numerous occasions. The Anna jeans' design features double belt loops that crisscross along the waistband to create a flattering illusion of a cinched silhouette. This clever detail is complemented by the back pockets, which add a touch of sophistication and balance out the overall look. The true magic of these jeans lies in how they can be styled to perfection, as seen in Kate Moss's effortless ensembles featuring white ballet flats that appear to be from Repetto's men's collection, paired with a navy three-quarter-zip jumper. The result is a chic, laid-back look that allows the wearer to seamlessly blend into Parisian streets like the Marais district. Vogue : https://www.vogue.com/article/wide-leg-french-girl-jeans

articles.title: Tom Holland and Zendaya Confirm Romantic Relationship

articles.content: Spider-Man co-stars Zendaya and Tom Holland confirmed their romantic relationship in 2021, putting an end to years of speculation about their personal lives. Their on-screen chemistry as Peter Parker and MJ had been building since they first met on set in 2016, but it wasn't until 2021 that the rumors of a real-life romance were officially confirmed. The couple's relationship has been shrouded in secrecy, with both actors keeping their private lives under wraps. However, their initial meeting on the Spider-Man set marked the beginning of a long-term connection that would eventually blossom into romance. In July 2016, Tom Holland was the first to share a photo of Zendaya on his social media platform, and soon they were frequently appearing in each other's Instagram feeds. As the months went by, it became increasingly clear that Zendaya and Tom Holland's friendship was blossoming into something more. The two had been paired together for numerous promotional events, including the Spider-Man: Homecoming premiere in June. In an interview with People before the premiere, Holland gushed about his friendship with Zendaya, highlighting their close bond. He described her as "so great and amazing, and shared a lighthearted moment when he joked about taking vacations together, despite having been unable to take one in years. For her part, Zendaya also spoke highly of Holland, calling him a great dude and one of her closest friends. She emphasized the importance of independence during young adulthood, explaining that it's difficult to be in a committed relationship when both partners are still figuring out life and making mistakes along the way. Zendaya noted that people often make poor decisions due to their limited experience and understanding of what's right and wrong. She stressed that individuals cannot change one another, and that relationships can be challenging when both parties are navigating uncharted territory. The timeline of Zendaya and Tom Holland's romance has been a subject of much speculation over the years. Although they were spotted together at the Oscars in March 2018, they walked the red carpet separately, suggesting that their relationship was still in its early stages. As the months went by, Zendaya attended high-profile events like the Met Gala in May 2018, where she wore a striking Joan of Arc-inspired Versace gown. Tom Holland took notice and posted a photo of her on his Instagram account, praising her with the caption All hail the queen. His admiration was likely intended to be lighthearted, but it sparked further rumors about their relationship. The following month, in June 2018, Zendaya made a playful gesture towards Tom Holland by posting a video of him goofing off with a lightsaber. The tongue-in-cheek message accompanying the clip read Me, myself and the birthday girl, which seemed to hint at her affection for the actor. However, she quickly clarified that she was not the one who had posted the comment. When asked about their relationship in June 2019, Tom Holland denied any romantic involvement with Zendaya, stating that he is single and looking for someone special. Interestingly, he described himself as definitely a relationship person, which could suggest that he values commitment and partnership in his relationships. The couple's relationship was still in its early stages when Tom Holland shared a mirror selfie of himself with Zendaya on set in September 2021. Zendaya marked her birthday that month with a post showcasing photos of herself on the red carpet at the Venice Film Festival, wearing a striking Balmain dress. It wasn't long before she stepped out again, this time alongside co-star Timothée Chalamet to promote the film Dune. The couple's relationship continued to blossom in early September when they celebrated Zendaya's 26th birthday together at MAMO Italian restaurant in Manhattan. The actress opted for a relaxed yet stylish look, pairing low-waisted denim jeans with a black crop top and long sleeves that were secured with a few buttons. Her co-stars from Euphoria also joined them for the celebration. Hunter Schafer was among those who attended the birthday gathering at MAMO Italian restaurant. The casual setting provided an opportunity for Zendaya to unwind and spend quality time with her loved ones, including Holland, who arrived dressed in a blue plaid button-down shirt and dark teal pants. His outfit was completed with white sneakers that added a touch of sportiness. In an interview shortly after winning the Emmy Award for her performance as Rue on Euphoria, Zendaya spoke about her relationship with Holland when asked who she texted first to share the news. She replied, Well, I didn’t have to text my mom because my mom was already there, she’s here tonight, which is very special. The question marked a brief moment of introspection for the actress. The celebration at MAMO Italian restaurant was not the only occasion when Zendaya and Holland were spotted together in September. They also had a low-key coffee date at Tatte on Boylston Street, where they seemed to be enjoying each other's company without drawing too much attention to themselves. Their visit to the Louvre in Paris last October was a subtle yet public display of affection. Zendaya and Holland strolled hand-in-hand through the museum's galleries, taking in the famous artwork on display. The casual atmosphere allowed them to be themselves without drawing too much attention. On that day, Zendaya sported a light blue blouse with her sleeves rolled up, her hair tied back in a bun with loose tendrils framing her face. Holland opted for a more understated look in a white and black striped shirt with long sleeves and black pants. His short hair was slightly tousled, adding to his effortless charm. As the months passed, fans noticed Holland resurfacing on social media after a summer break. The caption just zendaya owning the camera" aptly summarized the clip, highlighting Zendaya's confidence and poise. articles.title: Iranians Flee Homeland Amid Economic Turmoil and Conflict
articles.summary: A growing number of young Iranians are fleeing their homeland in search of better opportunities abroad due to the death of Jina Mahsa Amini, the US-Israel war with Iran, and economic mismanagement.
articles.content: A growing number of young Iranians are fleeing their homeland in search of better opportunities abroad. The decision to leave was triggered by a series of events, including the death in custody of 22-year-old Jina Mahsa Amini in 2022. The Iranian-Kurdish woman had been arrested for allegedly violating Iran's strict dress code, sparking widespread protests and inspiring the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement. Amini's death was a turning point for many young Iranians who felt that their future in the country was uncertain. They began to question the morality police's authority and the hijab mandate enforced by authorities. The physician, who wished to remain anonymous, explained that her decision to leave Iran was also influenced by the US-Israel war with Iran. She had been living with her family in a rented apartment in Turkey since early summer, hoping to eventually continue on to Germany. She had applied for an appointment at the German Embassy in Tehran two years ago but faced significant delays due to bureaucratic hurdles. Her professional qualifications were only recognized in Germany after a lengthy process. The escalating conflict in Iran has sparked a growing exodus of young talent from the country, with many seeking refuge in neighboring Turkey. Turkey's relaxed visa policy for Iranian citizens allows them to enter without a visa for up to 90 days, making it an attractive option for those fleeing the conflict. A significant number of Iranians have already crossed into Turkey since the latest conflict began, with thousands more attempting to secure their stay through residence permits rather than seeking asylum. Many of these individuals are skilled professionals and academics who hope to settle permanently in Europe or North America, disillusioned by Iran's war-hit economy and the prospect of little future there. The turmoil in Iran has been compounded by decades of sanctions and economic mismanagement, with a US naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Gulf disrupting oil exports, trade, and government revenues. The economic pressures imposed by sanctions and mismanagement have led to a decline in Iran's ability to provide its citizens with essential services. Basic necessities like food, housing, healthcare, and education are becoming increasingly unaffordable for many people. As a result of the worsening conditions, individuals are being forced to make difficult decisions about their future. Some, like physicians, are choosing to stay abroad until circumstances improve in Iran. However, others, including those who initially moved to Turkey, have decided to return home and submit new visa applications from within the country. The improved situation at the German embassy in Tehran has prompted some individuals to reconsider their plans for immigration. Unmarried friends of a physician, who had previously spent significant sums maintaining their stay in Turkey, are now returning to Iran to apply for visas from home. Many Iranians are weighing the risks and benefits of emigration, particularly those with family ties abroad. They must balance the uncertainty of waiting for family reunification visas against the possibility of new conflicts erupting in the region. The brain drain caused by the departure of highly qualified professionals and students has become a pressing concern for Iranian society as a whole. It's estimated that few families remain untouched by emigration, with many others considering leaving due to the dire economic situation. The University of Guilan's 2025 study on social participation and emigration intentions among Iranian students has shed light on a concerning trend. Researchers discovered a significant correlation between limited opportunities for shaping one's future in Iran and a higher likelihood of considering emigration. Economic concerns are not the sole driving force behind this trend, as many young Iranians feel constrained by their country's strict social and political environment. A sense of powerlessness and limited participation in decision-making processes have become major push factors for emigration. For some, securing a spot at a foreign university is already within reach. Mahsa, a mid-twenties student, has secured admission to a German university, paving the way for her departure from Iran. Others, like Ali, are taking steps towards leaving, with his long-term goal of obtaining a stronger qualification and eventually departing. Ali's plans are ambitious: he aims to secure a scholarship that will allow him to leave Iran in pursuit of a better future. Das's emotional moment was palpable as he displayed the handwritten note, highlighting the special bond between him and his daughter. The recovery by Bangladesh was nothing short of remarkable as they overcame a disastrous start to their innings. They put on 99 runs for the fourth wicket before Rabada struck again, sending Tanzid back to the pavilion after he had scored 67 off 108 deliveries. But Hridoy continued his impressive form in Test cricket, scoring his second century in just seven innings with a well-crafted 137 off 227 balls. His partnership with Litton Das was what turned the game around for Bangladesh as they began to put up a strong fight against their South African opponents. Das's recent performance in a match against the West Indies had been nothing short of exceptional, where he struck an impressive 224 runs. By that standard, his half-century on the first day was well within reach, and he achieved it off just 71 deliveries, leaving him unbeaten on 92 at the end of the day's play. It was only a matter of time before Das would go on to score a Test century against South Africa, becoming the third Bangladesh batter to achieve this milestone in the process. Das eventually fell for 120 runs after a well-crafted innings that included 14 fours and a six, caught by Marco Jansen off Dane Paterson's bowling. Paterson's impressive performance with the ball had been a key factor in restricting Bangladesh's scoring rate, and his four wickets for 92 runs will be a valuable contribution to South Africa's cause. In the end, it was a day that belonged to both Das and Paterson, as they left their mark on the proceedings with outstanding performances.
